content: 1. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur when co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Serious interactions may occur; alternative therapies are recommended. Co-administration with ethinylestradiol may alter hormone levels, and non-hormonal contraceptive methods are advised. 5. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of BCRP substrates. Do not exceed an ethinylestradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. 8. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of frovatriptan by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown; monitor closely. 9. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ethinylestradiol increases green tea levels by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of hemin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further reduce hemin efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of heparin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of hyaluronidase by rendering tissues partially resistant to its action. Larger doses of hyaluronidase may be required for equivalent effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 18. Iloperidone increases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ethinylestradiol may increase antidepressant serum concentrations by decreasing oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). This may lead to increased TCA adverse effects. Monitor closely. 20. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 21. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin (e.g., aspart, degludec, detemir, glargine, glulisine, lispro, NPH, regular human, inhaled) by pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially impairing glycemic control. Monitor diabetic patients closely. 22. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 23. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Monitor closely. 25. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 27. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Etonogestrel decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce lamotrigine plasma concentrations. Monitor closely. 29. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially impairing glycemic control. Monitor diabetic patients closely. 31. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Monitor closely. 32. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lomitapide doses should not exceed 30 mg/day. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor for arrhythmias. 34. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 response. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown; monitor closely. 36. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 37. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Lenolisib increases systemic exposure of BCRP substrates, including ethinylestradiol. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 39. Lesinurad decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 40. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of letrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 42. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
